title: The Sleeping Giant Quiz
description: Watched "The sleeping giant beneath the Malay Peninsula"? Test what you know about earthquakes in Malaysia.

questions.question: Which plate does Malaysia sit on?
options: Sundaland, part of the Eurasian Plate
questions.explanation: Malaysia sits in the core of Sundaland on the Eurasian Plate, far from plate boundaries, so large earthquakes are rare.

questions.question: Where do most of the big "outside" earthquakes felt in Malaysia come from?
questions.explanation: The Indo-Australian Plate dives beneath the Sunda Plate off Sumatra, and shaking from big quakes there can reach the Malay Peninsula.

questions.question: How did the 2004 Sumatra–Andaman earthquake affect faults in the Malay Peninsula?
options: It lifted the whole peninsula by hundreds of metres
It locked every fault in place
questions.explanation: The megaquake changed the stress across the region and is thought to have woken up some ancient faults that had been dormant.

questions.question: Which two faults in Peninsular Malaysia get the most attention as relatively active?
options: Sumatran Fault and Red River Fault
questions.explanation: The Bukit Tinggi and Kuala Lumpur faults are the most closely watched of the peninsula's potentially active faults.

questions.question: What made the Segamat earthquake unusual?
options: It was the biggest earthquake in Malaysian history
Its epicentre was not on any known fault zone
It was caused by a volcanic eruption
questions.explanation: An epicentre away from known fault zones suggests there may be structures underground we haven't found yet, so it needs more research.
